name: mcom-showcase
title: MCoM showcase: faithful phototroph-heterotroph community dynamics in process-bigraph
description:
Two studies exercise the same wrapped MCoM community (a single phytoplankton
and a single heterotroph coupled through DOC/DON pools and inorganic nitrogen)
under two contrasting environmental regimes, driven entirely by the clean-room
reproduction in viva_mcom.engine.
question:
Does the viva-mcom process-bigraph wrapper -- a clean-room NumPy reproduction
of the MCoM 1.0 Julia engine -- faithfully reproduce MCoM's phototroph-
heterotroph community dynamics, both in a closed batch co-culture and in an
open, seasonally-forced chemostat, while exposing the community as a composable
bigraph process?
hypothesis:
Because the reproduction is validated bit-for-bit against real MCoM Julia
output on deterministic configs, the wrapped composites should reproduce the
canonical microbial-community behaviours MCoM was built to capture: a
phytoplankton bloom that draws down nutrient and fuels a heterotroph through
its exudate (batch), and a sustained, seasonally-oscillating community under
continuous dilution and annual light forcing (chemostat).

executive.what_is_this:
viva-mcom wraps MCoM 1.0 (Lucken et al., GMD 2026) -- a scalable box model of
phototroph-heterotroph microbial communities whose numerical core is Julia --
as a process-bigraph process, via a clean-room NumPy reproduction that runs
with no Julia toolchain. This investigation demonstrates the wrapper on two
regimes: a closed batch co-culture and an open seasonally-lit chemostat.
executive.verdict:
The reproduction is faithful (bit-for-bit against real MCoM Julia output) and
both composites reproduce the expected community dynamics: all four behaviour
tests across the two studies pass.
executive.verdict_detail:
Fidelity: viva_mcom reproduces the upstream Julia engine to < 1e-9 (in fact
exactly) on the two shipped golden trajectories (tests/test_golden.py).
Batch co-culture: the phytoplankton blooms (0.01 -> 0.84 @ day 44) and busts;
the heterotroph rises on the exudate to a peak 2.39 @ day 50 -- a ~7-day lag
behind the bloom, the exudate-consumption signature -- for a run-mean density
of 0.74 (>200x its inoculum); inorganic nitrogen is drawn down from 8.8 mM to
a second-half mean of 1.87 mM. Seasonal chemostat: the community is sustained
under 0.1/day dilution, with phytoplankton oscillating 0.42-0.89 (2.1x
peak/trough) on the annual light cycle and holding DIN near 2.1 mM against a
10 mM inflow. Both studies pass all declared behaviour tests.

scientific_argument.main_claim:
viva-mcom faithfully reproduces MCoM 1.0's phototroph-heterotroph community
dynamics as a composable process-bigraph process, across both closed-batch
and open-chemostat regimes.
evidence_for: Bit-for-bit reproduction of the upstream MCoM Julia engine on two golden trajectories (tests/test_golden.py, agreement exactly 0).
Batch co-culture reproduces the canonical bloom-bust succession with a heterotroph that grows only on phytoplankton exudate and lags the bloom by ~7 days (study mcom-coculture, both tests pass).
Seasonally-forced chemostat produces a sustained, annually-oscillating community (2.1x peak/trough) that neither washes out nor runs away (study mcom-seasonal, both tests pass).
caveats: This is a clean-room reproduction, not the upstream Julia engine; RNG-dependent random parameter/network draws are not reproduced (deterministic configs are exact). See REPRODUCTION.md.
Both studies use the shipped 1-phytoplankton / 1-heterotroph parameter set; MCoM's scalability to large communities is supported by the framework but not exercised here.

studies.name: mcom-coculture
studies.title: MCoM co-culture: a phytoplankton bloom feeds a heterotroph
studies.question:
In a closed (batch) box seeded with a single phytoplankton and a single
heterotroph population, does the MCoM reproduction produce the canonical
phototroph-heterotroph succession -- a phytoplankton bloom that draws down
inorganic nitrogen and, through its exuded dissolved organic carbon and
nitrogen, fuels the growth of a heterotroph that would otherwise have almost
no substrate?

studies.name: mcom-seasonal
studies.title: MCoM under seasonal light: a sustained, oscillating chemostat community
studies.question:
When the same MCoM phytoplankton-heterotroph pair is placed in an open,
dilution-driven box (a chemostat) with a steady nutrient inflow but a
sinusoidally varying, annual light supply, does the community reach a
sustained regime that blooms and recedes with the seasons rather than washing
out or running to a fixed point?
